Thanks Alice — good questions. High-level guidance based on our internal trade studies and customer benchmarks:

- AWQ (4-bit variants)
  - Pros: largest memory savings and lowest GPU RAM requirements; great for fitting model on cheaper instances or on-prem constrained GPUs.
  - Cons: can show small but measurable quality regressions on nuanced generation tasks and classification thresholds — we typically observe a 1.5-4% delta on intent accuracy for 7B class models depending on prompt sensitivity.

- GPTQ (post-training quantization)
  - Pros: generally better fidelity vs aggressive AWQ in our experience, with lower quality loss on classification/semantic tasks.
  - Cons: slightly larger model size than AWQ and sometimes slower token throughput depending on kernel support.

- FP8 (mixed-precision float8 paths)
  - Pros: higher throughput on supported hardware (A100/H100 with new runtimes), good for high qps inference where latency per-token matters.
  - Cons: requires hardware/runtime support; can introduce small numerical differences — usually <2% quality delta on our tests but varies with model and prompt.

Quick recommendation for FinWave's use case (realtime summarization + tight latency):
- Start with Redwood-7B-GPTQ for a quality-first baseline.
- Parallel AWQ run for a cost-optimized comparison — check intent accuracy against GT.
- If throughput is still a bottleneck and you have A100/H100 in Dedicated, try Redwood-13B-FP8 as a throughput experiment.

I've attached the trade study PDF and a short spreadsheet with benchmark links (public for now). Also included a short note on tuning knobs (KV cache warmup, batching windows, and prefix caching) that will help maintain latency.

Attachments: [attachment: quantization-tradeoffs-AWQ-GPTQ-FP8.pdf]
Drive benchmarks: https://drive.google.com/finwave-eval-benchmarks

I'll put together the hosted eval plan and sample HubSpot checklist today.

—Marissa
